newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND UNDONE BY ALL BLACK NEW WAVE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND UNDONE BY ALL BLACK NEW WAVE.

text.p: England were given a glimpse of the latest wave of All Black talent as they tumbled to a 34-19 defeat against the New Zealand Barbarians at Twickenham on Saturday.

Despite leading 19-13 early in the second-half, the home side were undone by a late flurry of New Zealand scoring masterminded by Auckland fly-half Carlos Spencer who has yet to make his All Black test debut.

The 21-year-old Spencer scored a memorable individual try with seven minutes left to settle an exciting encounter and also kicked two penalties and a conversion to ensure a more comfortable margin of victory than had looked probable.

The game, marking the 125th anniversary of the Rugby Football Union, had been billed as the perfect opportunity for England to gain some revenge for their humiliation at the hands of Jonah Lomu in the World Cup last year.

Lomu, passed fit only hours before kick-off, irnonically had a subdued game, touching the ball only twice in the second-half and leaving the stage clear for emerging stars such as Spencer and full-back Christian Cullen.

Cullen was a constant handful but England still held a slightly fortunate 9-8 lead at half-time thanks to three penalties from Mike Catt, the chief victim of Lomu's awesome power in his side's fateful Cape Town semifinal.

Robin Brooke scored the only try of the first-half after just six minutes, capitalising on a quick throw from Joeli Vidiri, and the New Zealanders again reacted quickest at the start of the second half.

Flanker Andrew Blowers raced over to capitalise on a break from Andrew Mehrtens with less than 50 seconds gone, only for two tries in five minutes from winger Jon Sleightholme and full-back Tim Stimpson to give England fresh heart.
No New Zealand side, let alone one led by Sean Fitzpatrick and containing 13 All Blacks, fades in the closing stages and the Barbarians, despite their unfamiliar red jerseys, proved no exeception.
The English forwards, so conspicuous in the first hour, began to tire and successful penalties from Mehrtens and Spencer dragged the score back to 19-19.

Spencer's dancing feet and another late score from Vidiri on the right wing duly reasserted New Zealand dominance. The scoreline might have been even less flattering to England had either Fitzpatrick or Michael Jones not been denied first-half tries by an alert referee.
"We all knew the game would be an 80-minute one and so it proved," said Sleightholme. "They are the best side in the world."

England - 15-Tim Stimpson; 14-Jon Sleightholme, 13-Will Carling, 12-Phil de Glanville (captain), 11-Adedayo Adebayo; 10- Mike Catt, 9-Andy Gomarsall; 8-Chris Sheasby, 7-Lawrence Dallaglio, 6-Tim Rodber, 5-Simon Shaw, 4-Martin Johnson, 3-Jason Leonard, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.

New Zealand Barbarians - 15-Christian Cullen; 14-Joeli Vidiri (16-Glen Osborne, 79th), 13-Alama Ieremia, 12-Lee Stensness, 11-Jonah Lomu; 10-Andrew Mehrtens (17-Carlos Spencer, 59th), 9-Justin Marshall; 8-Taine Randell (20-Dylan Mika, 56th), 7-Andrew Blowers, 6-Michael Jones, 5-Robin Brooke, 4-Ian Jones, 3-Olo Brown, 2-Sean Fitzpatrick, 1-Mark Allen.
